title: Reflection of coherence by a coherent conservative inverse image
statement: Let $u:\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E$ be a coherent conservative geometric morphism between coherent Grothendieck topoi, with all these terms defined in [def-trf-coherent-topos]. For every object $A\in\mathcal E$, if $u^{-1}A$ is coherent in $\mathcal E'$, then $A$ is coherent in $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Author draft, §8.1, printed p. 17, paragraph beginning with the coherence of a constructible sheaf: reflection of coherence by a coherent conservative morphism. Read online; local archival copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Work in small-site presentations of the two topoi from [def-trf-coherent-topos]. For a small family of set sheaves $(T_i)$, form the presheaf $P(U)=\coprod_iT_i(U)$, with restrictions retaining the index. Maps from $P$ to any presheaf are exactly families of maps from the $T_i$, by restriction to the summands. Thus [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] identifies $P^\#$ with the coproduct in sheaves. The unit $P\to P^\#$ sheafifies to an isomorphism by the same universal property; [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] therefore implies that each section of this coproduct locally comes from one summand. This construction and argument include the empty family.

source.place: Tags 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint), 00WI (lemma-colimit-sheaves), 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification); the coproduct universal property is written out here.

proof.text: By Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective], a family $(T_i\to T)$ has epimorphic coproduct map exactly when every section of $T$ locally lifts to one $T_i$. This criterion is stable under base change: for $R\to T$ and a section $r$ of $R$, locally lift its image in $T$ to $t_i$; then $(r,t_i)$ is a section of $R\times_TT_i$. The fibre product has these pairs as its sections by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise]. Composing two such covering families amounts to doing these local lifts successively, and the transitivity axiom of a site combines the coverings. We will use this covering calculus below.

source.place: Tag 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf), and the covering transitivity axiom; direct local-section argument.

proof.text: Write $F=u^{-1}$. By [def-trf-coherent-topos], $F$ has a right adjoint and preserves finite limits. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], it preserves small coproducts and coequalizers. Every epimorphism in a set-sheaf topos is a coequalizer of its kernel pair by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-kernel-pair-coequalizer]. Its image under $F$ is consequently a coequalizer, hence an epimorphism (two maps agreeing after the coequalizer arrow are equal by its uniqueness clause). Therefore $F$ preserves covering families, using its coproduct comparison.

source.place: Tag 086K (lemma-coequalizer-surjection), together with Categories Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact), part (1); applied to the inverse-image adjunction.

proof.text: The functor $F$ is faithful: if $F(a)=F(b)$, the image of an equalizer $e$ of $a,b$ is an equalizer of two equal arrows, hence is invertible. Conservativity makes $e$ invertible, and $ae=be$ gives $a=b$. Equalizers exist by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise]. Now if $F(p)$ is epi and $ap=bp$, applying $F$ gives $F(a)=F(b)$ and faithfulness gives $a=b$. Thus $F$ reflects epimorphisms, and, since it preserves coproducts by Step 3, it reflects covering families as well.

source.place: Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf) for equalizers; the remaining argument is the universal property of the equalizer, conservativity and right cancellation.

proof.text: For any object $T$ of $\mathcal E$, quasi-compactness of $F(T)$ implies quasi-compactness of $T$. Indeed, take any small covering family $(T_i\to T)_{i\in I}$ in the definition [def-trf-coherent-topos]. By Step 3 its image covers $F(T)$. Quasi-compactness gives a finite $J\subseteq I$ for which $(F(T_j)\to F(T))_{j\in J}$ covers. By Step 4 the original finite subfamily covers $T$. This is exactly the definition of quasi-compactness and does not assume that $T$ or the $T_i$ are coherent.

source.place: Agent expansion of the quasi-compactness part of the reflection assertion in §8.1, printed p. 17.

proof.text: We also need preservation of quasi-compact objects. First, in either topos a finite covering family of quasi-compact objects $(Q_j\to Q)_{j\in J}$ has quasi-compact target: pull any cover $(R_i\to Q)$ back to each $Q_j$ by Step 2, choose a finite set $I_j$ of indices covering $Q_j$, and take $I_0=\bigcup_{j\in J}I_j$. The composite covering of $Q$ factors through $(R_i\to Q)_{i\in I_0}$, which is therefore covering. This is a finite union argument directly from [def-trf-coherent-topos]; when $J$ is empty the same factorization uses the empty cover.

source.place: Agent expansion of §8.1, printed p. 17: elementary finite-cover quasi-compactness calculation, using the local covering calculus of Step 2.

proof.text: If $B$ is any quasi-compact object of $\mathcal E$, the coherent generators in [def-trf-coherent-topos] give a small covering family $(G_i\to B)$ with coherent $G_i$. Choose a finite subcover using quasi-compactness of $B$. Step 3 sends it to a finite cover of $F(B)$. Coherence of $u$ makes each $F(G_i)$ coherent, hence quasi-compact by definition. Step 6 now gives quasi-compactness of $F(B)$. We have not assumed that quasi-compact objects themselves are coherent.

source.place: Agent expansion of §8.1, printed p. 17: finite coherent-generator cover and coherence of inverse image.

proof.text: By hypothesis $F(A)$ is coherent, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated in the sense of [def-trf-coherent-topos]. Step 5 gives quasi-compactness of $A$. For quasi-separatedness, let $B\to A$ and $C\to A$ have arbitrary quasi-compact sources. Step 7 gives quasi-compactness of $F(B)$ and $F(C)$, so quasi-separatedness of $F(A)$ makes $F(B)\times_{F(A)}F(C)$ quasi-compact. Finite-limit preservation identifies this object with $F(B\times_A C)$. Step 5 implies that $B\times_A C$ is quasi-compact. As $B,C$ were arbitrary, this proves quasi-separatedness of $A$; together with quasi-compactness, it proves coherence of $A$.

source.place: Agent expansion of the coherent-conservative reflection assertion in §8.1, printed p. 17, using its quasi-compact and quasi-separated terminology.
